change.title: pr-1-flat
change.description: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the audit log's datetime key
findings.body: The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime` (`organization_auditlogs.py:80`), a DateTimeField. `get_item_key` here is copied from `Paginator` (integer keys): `math.floor(value)` on a `datetime` raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls the key function on the first result (`utils/cursors.py:122`, `137`), so any non-empty page with `?optimized_pagination=true` returns a 500. `value_from_cursor` (line 843) also returns the raw cursor value. `DateTimePaginator` converts it back to a datetime (`paginator.py:238-241`). Here `build_queryset` would compare the `datetime` column to a millisecond integer. The existing `DateTimePaginator` handles both conversions, so the new class should subclass it, or reuse its key and value logic. Nothing else in the repo uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and there are no tests, so the broken path ships unnoticed.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch passes a negative slice start to a Django queryset, which raises
findings.body: `Cursor.from_string` accepts any integer offset, including negative (`utils/cursors.py:59`). With `enable_advanced_features`, a cursor like `0:-5:0` reaches `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset` (lines 880-882). Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The user gets a 500. The comments claim 'Django ORM properly handles negative slicing' and that this grants 'access to data beyond normal pagination bounds'. The first is false. The second describes a feature the code cannot deliver, and it would be a data-exposure risk if it worked. The stated 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' does not hold for this paginator: it only receives the already-filtered queryset. Remove the branch and clamp or reject negative offsets instead.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator behavior change is inconsistent and its comment is misleading
findings.body: This edit changes `BasePaginator.get_result`, used by every `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator` endpoint, not just audit logs. A negative offset on a forward cursor is now silently clamped to 0, so a crafted cursor returns the first page instead of an error. A negative offset on a prev cursor still goes through unclamped (`if not cursor.is_prev else offset`) and still hits the Django negative-index assertion. The comment says negative offsets are allowed 'for efficient bidirectional pagination', but the code clamps the forward case and does not support the prev case. Line 192 (`len(results) == offset + limit + extra`) still uses the unclamped `offset`. If the aim is to harden against negative offsets, clamp for both directions, or reject them in `Cursor.from_string`. Otherwise revert this hunk, since it is unrelated to the new paginator.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result wholesale
findings.body: `get_result` (lines 845-911) is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result`. The only difference is the negative-offset branch, which is broken (see the other finding). The class docstring promises 'optimized query path' and 'streamlined boundary handling', but there is no optimization. Future fixes to the base would need to be made twice. If a variant is really needed, override a small hook instead of copying the method.

findings.title: Gate uses `is_superuser` rather than an active superuser session, and the gate hides a broken feature
findings.body: `request.user.is_superuser` is the account flag. It does not check that the user has an active superuser session, which Sentry normally verifies with `is_active_superuser(request)`. Any org member with `has_global_access` also passes, so the 'authorized administrators' framing is broader than stated. `organization_context.member` is also dereferenced for non-superusers, so it must be non-None. The paginator behind the gate exposes nothing useful today, because it errors (see the paginator findings). Prefer dropping the opt-in query parameter until the paginator works. Lines 71 and 89 also have trailing whitespace.

findings.title: No tests for the new query parameter, paginator or cursor handling
findings.body: The PR adds a new public query parameter (`optimized_pagination`), a new paginator class and a change to shared pagination, with no tests. A test of `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` with `optimized_pagination=true` would have caught the `TypeError` in `get_item_key`. Tests for negative cursor offsets, covering both paginators, are also missing.

findings.title: Comment on Cursor.offset claims support for negative offsets that does not exist
findings.body: The comment says `Cursor` allows negative offsets 'for advanced pagination scenarios' and 'efficient reverse pagination'. `Cursor` has not changed (`int(offset)` already accepted negatives), and no consumer handles a negative offset: Django slicing rejects it. The comment misleads readers of a core class. Remove it.

contracts.action: GET audit logs with optimized_pagination=true routes to OptimizedCursorPaginator
contracts.equivalent_path: Default branch using DateTimePaginator (organization_auditlogs.py:85-91; DateTimePaginator at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:230-241)
contracts.before_after: The default path converts the datetime key to milliseconds and converts the cursor value back to a datetime. The new path uses Paginator-style integer key handling (paginator.py:838-843) and does neither conversion.
contracts.visible_effect: Admins or superusers who pass the parameter get a 500 on any non-empty page, because math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError.
contracts.failure_mode: The exception propagates from build_cursor to the endpoint, which has no handling for it, so the request fails with a 500. A negative cursor offset also raises Django's negative-indexing AssertionError.

contracts.before_after: Before, any negative offset reached the queryset slice and raised. Now forward cursors are clamped to 0 and prev cursors are passed through unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: Crafted forward cursors with negative offsets silently return the first page instead of an error. Prev cursors still return a 500. This applies to every endpoint using BasePaginator subclasses.
contracts.failure_mode: Inconsistent handling between forward and prev cursors.

summary: The opt-in `optimized_pagination=true` path on the audit log endpoint is broken. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` uses integer key handling on a datetime field, so any non-empty page raises a TypeError (500). Its negative-offset branch would also hit Django's negative-indexing assertion. The change also edits shared `BasePaginator` behavior inconsistently: forward cursors are clamped and prev cursors are not. The comments claim capabilities the code doesn't have, `get_result` is duplicated wholesale, the admin gate uses `is_superuser` rather than an active superuser session, and there are no tests.
